card: Adds an optional build-time script tracer to libbitcoinkernel that emits snapshots of script evaluation state at start, exit, and per opcode. External applications using the kernel library currently have no way to inspect intermediate script execution state to build script debuggers or execution monitors. The author provides a proof-of-concept debugger using rust-bitcoinkernel and notes potential benefits for interpreter unit tests and fuzzing to catch cases where errors shadow unexpected interpreter behavior. The feature is disabled by default via a compile-time cmake flag and requires no prerequisite pull requests.
changed_since_previous: No substantive architectural changes; the implementation remains gated behind ENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE with the same C API surface and EvalScript trace hooks.
evidence: Author provides an external proof-of-concept branch showcasing a rudimentary script debugger built on rust-bitcoinkernel: 'The initial sketch for this work was prepared on rust-bitcoinkernel: https://github.com/sedited/rust-bitcoinkernel/tree/feature_script_debug . That branch also includes a very rudimentary script debugger showcasing the use case for this patch.'

Author cites PR #33961 as an example of testing pitfalls: 'ensure that the script interpreter is actually doing what we think it is doing during the script tests. This might prevent unit test bugs in the future, i.e. when error conditions shadow actual behaviour'
problem: External applications using libbitcoinkernel cannot observe step-by-step script evaluation to build tools like script debuggers or fine-grained execution analyzers. In addition, script interpreter unit tests and fuzzers have limited visibility into intermediate interpreter state, making it difficult to detect cases where unexpected behavior is shadowed by a subsequent error.

risk.why: A mistake introduced directly inside EvalScript could alter script evaluation semantics or crash nodes during block validation, leading to consensus divergence.

scope_notes: Touches the core script execution loop in EvalScript (src/script/interpreter.cpp), though the hooks expand to static_assert(true) when the cmake option ENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE is OFF.
summary: Adds an optional build-time script evaluation tracer exposed through the libbitcoinkernel C API and its C++ wrapper. Gated behind the compile-time flag ENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE, EvalScript emits trace frame snapshots at execution start, exit, and before each opcode execution. Downstream consumers can register a callback to inspect intermediate execution state, including stack and altstack contents, current opcode, execution flag, op counter, signature version, and script errors.
